definitionText: BPH is a non-cancerous enlargement of the prostate gland commonly seen in men above 40–50 years of age. causes: Age-related hormonal changes in men; family history of prostate problems; obesity and sedentary lifestyle; diabetes, high blood pressure, or heart disease; smoking and excessive alcohol intake.

definitionText: Urinary Stones are hard deposits made of minerals and salts that form in the kidneys, ureter (tube connecting kidney to bladder), or bladder. symptoms: Sudden, severe pain in the side, back, lower abdomen, or groin
Burning sensation or pain while passing urine
Blood in urine (pink, red, or brown discoloration)
Frequent urge to urinate, but passing small amounts
Nausea, vomiting, or restlessness during pain episodes
Fever and chills (if infection is present)
causes: Less water intake and dehydration; high salt, high protein, or high oxalate diet; family history of kidney/urinary stones; recurrent urinary tract infections; certain medical conditions (like high uric acid, metabolic disorders); sedentary lifestyle and obesity.

treatmentOptions.title: Medical Management (for Small Stones)
treatmentOptions.description: Pain relief medications to control stone pain (renal colic), medicines to relax urinary tract muscles and help small stones pass naturally, antibiotics if there is associated infection, and increased water intake with dietary advice.

treatmentOptions.title: ESWL (Shock Wave Lithotripsy)
treatmentOptions.description: A non-invasive procedure where sound/shock waves are used to break stones into small fragments from outside the body, usually used for small to medium-sized kidney stones; stone pieces then pass naturally through urine over time.

treatmentOptions.title: URS (Ureteroscopy) / RIRS (Retrograde Intra-Renal Surgery)
treatmentOptions.description: A thin endoscope is passed through the urine passage (urethra and bladder) into the ureter or kidney; stones are visualized directly and broken using laser, then removed, with no major cut on the body — minimally invasive and fast recovery.

treatmentOptions.title: PCNL (Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy)
treatmentOptions.description: Recommended for large or multiple kidney stones. A small keyhole is made in the back to access the kidney directly; stones are broken and removed using special instruments; effective for complex or large stone burden.

treatmentOptions.title: Cystolithotripsy (for Bladder Stones)
treatmentOptions.description: Endoscopic procedure to break and remove stones from the bladder using laser or other energy sources.
